page: Microsoft Azure D16a_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DAv4 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7452 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 16 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, resulting in 2.0 threads per core. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.35 GHz and includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 410 GB of bundled local storage. There are no GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses included.

Benchmark data indicates balanced performance across most workloads. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25% with a score of 2707.27, while multi-core performance falls in the middle 50% average tier at 21649.45. Memory bandwidth tests show average read performance, with 799.89 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 52.64 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, a notable performance tradeoff is observed in large-block uncached memory write bandwidth, which is weak at 25.81 GB/sec, placing in the bottom 25% of tested systems.

For application workloads, the server demonstrates average capabilities. It achieves 14.43 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and a static web serving throughput of 9.81 GB/sec. Large language model inference speeds for a small 135M model are strong for text generation at 276.2 tokens/sec, but average for prompt processing at 826.52 tokens/sec. The qualitative cost efficiency of this hardware profile is defined by its balanced resource density, making it suitable for general-purpose workloads, web serving, software compilation, and database operations that do not require high-write memory bandwidth.
